records.label: Patient
quotes: A patient is described with a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme, malonyl CoA decarboxylase - an inborn error of metabolism not recognized previously.
The enzyme defect was first suspected because of persistent excretion of malonic and methylmalonic acids in urine in a child with repeated episodes of vomiting, some requiring hospitalization.
Disturbances of lipid metabolism were demonstrated.

records.label: Second child with MCD deficiency

phenotypes.text: malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity 4% of control in fibroblasts

quotes: He is mildly mentally retarded and presented with vomiting, a seizure, hypoglycaemia and mild metabolic acidosis during a urinary tract infection.
The urine contained increased amounts of malonic, methylmalonic, succinic, adipic, glutaric and suberic acids.
Mitochondrial malonyl CoA decarboxylase activity in cultured fibroblast extracts was 4% of the mean control value.

records.label: Two Scots-born patients

phenotypes.hpo_label: Febrile seizure (within the age range of 3 months to 6 years)

quotes: The new cases are Scots born and are the offspring of consanguinous parents of Scots/Irish origin. They were investigated during episodes of vomiting and febrile convulsions associated with concomitant developmental delay.
Malonic aciduria and grossly reduced malonyl CoA decarboxylase activity were demonstrated

records.label: Patient with S148X
quotes: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.
The first mutation is a 442C-->G transversion resulting in a premature stop codon (S148X) in the N-terminal half of the protein.
Both mutations were found to segregate appropriately within the families and were not found in 100 normal unrelated individuals.

quotes: The second is a 13-bp insertion in the mature RNA, causing a frameshift with predicted protein truncation. This insertion is the result of an intronic mutation generating a novel splice acceptor sequence (IVS4-14A-->G).
Both mutations were found to segregate appropriately within the families and were not found in 100 normal unrelated individuals.

Our patient has strikingly low appetite

records.label: Nine patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency
quotes: Clinical, biochemical and molecular characteristics of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency and long-term follow-up of nine patients.

notes.statement: In a girl with MCD deficiency, de Wit et al. (2006) found normal genomic MLYCD sequence but no MLYCD messenger product, suggesting an abnormality of transcription regulation.
quotes: MLYCD-gene sequence analysis shows normal genomic sequence but no messenger product, suggesting an abnormality of transcription regulation.

notes.statement: de Wit et al. (2006) recommended that patients with MCD deficiency be evaluated with brain MRI and that unexplained malformations of cortical development prompt metabolic screening.
quotes: patients with MCD deficiency should be evaluated with brain MRI and unexplained malformations of cortical development should be reason for metabolic screening.

notes.statement: Wightman et al. (2003) described MLYCD deficiency as an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy.
quotes: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy.

notes.statement: Wightman et al. (2003) identified 16 of 18 pathogenic MLYCD alleles by genomic sequencing in 9 unrelated patients with MLYCD deficiency. Western blot of patient fibroblasts (8 of these patients and 2 previously reported patients with homozygous mutations) using C-terminal antisera showed the 66-kDa band absent in 6 patients and substantially reduced in 3; 1 patient showed increased protein with a smeary 68-83-kDa band.
quotes: Genomic sequencing of MLYCD in nine unrelated patients identified 16 of 18 pathogenic alleles
Western blot analysis using antisera raised to a C-terminal peptide detected a 66-kDa band that was absent in six patients and substantially reduced in three patients.
One patient showed an increase in protein levels with a prominent smeary 68-l83-kDa band.

notes.statement: Wightman et al. (2003) found that the N-terminal mutation p.G3D mislocalized MLYCD to the plasma membrane, suggesting a novel targeting signal in a 4-amino acid conserved N-terminal motif, whereas a 25-base deletion between the putative mitochondrial and peroxisomal initiation codons (M1 and M40) and the p.M40T mutation showed punctate perinuclear staining. Because none of these mutations was predicted to alter catalytic function, they concluded that correct subcellular localization of MLYCD is likely critical for normal function.
quotes: An extreme N-terminal mutation c.8G>A (p.G3D) mislocalized to the plasma membrane, suggesting that a novel targeting signal may reside in a four-amino acid conserved N-terminal motif.

As none of the three mislocalizing mutations are predicted to alter the catalytic function of the peptide, it seems likely that correct subcellular localization of MLYCD is critical for it to function normally.

notes.statement: Sacksteder et al. (1999) described malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency as a lethal disorder characterized by cardiomyopathy and developmental delay, with phenotypes reminiscent of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders.
quotes: malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency, a lethal disorder characterized by cardiomyopathy and developmental delay
malonyl-CoA decarboxylase-deficient patients display a number of phenotypes that are reminiscent of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders

notes.statement: Sacksteder et al. (1999) identified a candidate human MCD gene through a computer-based search for peroxisomal proteins; the encoded protein carries a canonical type-1 peroxisomal targeting signal (SKL), and recombinant MCD had high intrinsic malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity. Subcellular fractionation showed that MCD resides in both the cytoplasm and peroxisomes.
quotes: A computer-based search for novel peroxisomal proteins led to the identification of a candidate gene for human MCD, which encodes a protein with a canonical type-1 peroxisomal targeting signal of serine-lysine-leucine(COOH).
We observed that recombinant MCD protein has high intrinsic malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity
Subcellular fractionation experiments revealed that MCD resides in both the cytoplasm and peroxisomes.

notes.statement: Sacksteder et al. (1999) proposed that cytoplasmic MCD regulates cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA abundance and thus mitochondrial fatty acid uptake and oxidation, and that peroxisomal MCD may degrade intraperoxisomal malonyl-CoA generated by peroxisomal beta-oxidation of odd chain-length dicarboxylic fatty acids. MCD mRNA was most abundant in cardiac and skeletal muscle.
quotes: Cytoplasmic MCD is positioned to play a role in the regulation of cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA abundance and, thus, of mitochondrial fatty acid uptake and oxidation.
MCD mRNA is most abundant in cardiac and skeletal muscles
we propose that this enzyme may be involved in degrading intraperoxisomal malonyl-CoA, which is generated by the peroxisomal beta-oxidation of odd chain-length dicarboxylic fatty acids

notes.statement: FitzPatrick et al. (1999) identified homozygous truncating mutations in the MCD gene in 2 consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency by RT-PCR of fibroblast RNA. Neither mutation was found in 100 normal unrelated individuals, which confirmed the cloned transcript as the human MCD ortholog.
quotes: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.
These mutations would be predicted to cause MCD deficiency, thus confirming this transcript as the hMCD ortholog.

notes.statement: FitzPatrick et al. (1999) found a C-terminal peroxisomal targeting sequence (-SKL) in human MCD. Subcellular fractionation of rat liver homogenates strongly suggested that MCD activity was localized to peroxisomes as well as to mitochondria.
quotes: The peptide sequence of hMCD revealed a C-terminal peroxisomal targeting sequence (-SKL).
strongly suggests that MCD is localized to peroxisomes in addition to the mitochondrial localization reported elsewhere

notes.statement: Gao et al. (1999) identified human malonyl-CoA decarboxylase cDNA sequences by homology to the goose gene. The 1,479-bp human cDNA was 70% identical to the goose sequence.
quotes: Human malonyl CoA decarboxylase cDNA sequences were identified by homology to the goose gene
The 1479 basepair human cDNA is 70 percent identical to the goose sequence

notes.statement: Gao et al. (1999) found the intron/exon boundaries of the human malonyl-CoA decarboxylase gene by directly sequencing a PAC clone that contained the entire gene. The boundaries were completely conserved between human and goose.
quotes: the intron/exon boundaries were determined by direct sequencing of a PAC clone containing the entire human gene
the intron/exon boundaries are completely conserved between the two species

notes.statement: Gao et al. (1999) noted that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency had been associated with mild mental retardation, seizures, hypotonia, cardiomyopathy, vomiting, hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and malonic aciduria.
quotes: deficiency of the enzyme has been associated with mild mental retardation, seizures, hypotonia, cardiomyopathy, vomiting, hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and malonic aciduria

notes.statement: MacPhee et al. (1993) noted that before their report, worldwide experience of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency had been limited to 2 affected Australian children.
quotes: Hitherto, the worldwide experience of the disorder has been confined to reports on two affected Australian children.

notes.statement: MacPhee et al. (1993) presented total ion current chromatograms of urinary organic acid profiles obtained by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
quotes: the total ion current chromatograms of urinary organic acid profiles obtained by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry are presented

notes.statement: Brown et al. (1984) described deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme malonyl-CoA decarboxylase as a previously unrecognized inborn error of metabolism. They first suspected it because a child persistently excreted malonic and methylmalonic acids in the urine.
quotes: A patient is described with a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme, malonyl CoA decarboxylase - an inborn error of metabolism not recognized previously.
The enzyme defect was first suspected because of persistent excretion of malonic and methylmalonic acids in urine

notes.statement: Haan et al. (1986) found that in their patient, a high fat, low carbohydrate diet caused symptomatic hypoglycemia, moderate metabolic acidosis, and urinary excretion of large amounts of organic acids and 3-hydroxybutyrate. An isocaloric low fat, high carbohydrate diet led to excretion of only relatively small amounts of malonic, methylmalonic and succinic acids. Acute fat and lysine loads increased urinary malonic acid without affecting the other organic acids.
quotes: A high fat, low carbohydrate diet led to symptomatic hypoglycaemia, a moderate metabolic acidosis and excretion in the urine of large amounts of the same organic acids and 3-hydroxybutyrate.
Only relatively small quantities of malonic, methylmalonic and succinic acid were excreted in the urine when the boy was fed an isocaloric low fat, high carbohydrate diet.
Acute fat and lysine loads led to increased excretion of malonic acid in the urine without affecting the excretion of the other organic acids.

notes.statement: Haan et al. (1986) suggested that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase serves an important mitochondrial function by preventing malonyl-CoA accumulation, and that its importance is most apparent when fat is the main metabolic fuel.
quotes: Experience with this patient suggests that malonyl CoA decarboxylase serves an important function in the mitochondrion by preventing accumulation of malonyl CoA.
The importance of the enzyme is best seen when fat is the main metabolic fuel.
